newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends up on commercial demand.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends up on commercial demand.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures closed higher on commercial buying as end-users were said seeking supplies in the futures due to tight stocks in the marketing pipeline, traders said.
"There's commercial buying in meal," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Cargill Inc, Continental Grain, Farmers Commodities Corp and Produce Grain each were noted purchasers of the January and March contracts, the traders said.
The commercial demand occurred a near-dearth of selling interest in the market.
"There was nothing for sale in meal," a trader said.
Soyoil found support from the really in the soybean pit and on commercial demand. Cargill Inc bought 900 lots of December soyoil, traders said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 26,000 contracts, up from 23,615 Friday, according to the CBOT. Soyoil volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, down from 16,324 Friday.
Soymeal closed $0.70 to $2.30 per ton higher, with December up $2.30 at $218.50. Soyoil was 0.01 to 0.17 cent per lb higher, with December up 0.01 at 22.74.
